cases.statement: Three batch rows, all male, in two papers from the same hospital (Jining). 33530800 case 1 (zygosity not stated) and case 2 (hemizygous); 37215540 proband Ⅲ-1 (zygosity not stated). The coordinator should check whether case 1 and Ⅲ-1 are the same person (see concerns).

people.label: case 1
people.zygosity_or_genotype: carrier; zygosity not stated (male, X-linked gene)
people.key_phenotypes: HCM progressing to dilated phase; WPW syndrome; mild intellectual disability and learning difficulty; autophagic vacuoles on endomyocardial biopsy; sudden cardiac death at 23

quotes.quote: A 23-year-old man had Danon disease from the age of 12 years, when symptoms began, until 23 years old when he succumbed to his disease.
He had suffered from a poor ability of physical activity, mild mental retardation, and learning difficulty.
ECG showed type B Wolff–Parkinson–White (WPW) syndrome, a high voltage in the left ventricle, and an inverted T wave (Figure 1a).
An endomyocardial biopsy and electron microscopic examination showed autophagic vacuoles.
In the next 4 years, HCM progressed to the dilated phase.
he finally succumbed to his disease with sudden cardiac arrest

people.label: case 2
people.key_phenotypes: WPW syndrome; left ventricular hypertrophy (HCM); raised CK and liver enzymes; intellectual disability

quotes.quote: A Chinese boy has been followed up from 10 years old.
Genetic analysis at 10 years old showed that he had Danon disease and was hemizygous for an LAMP-2 mutation, c.257_258delCC, in exon 3 of LAMP-2.

Biomarker levels were also considerably elevated (CK: 1986 U/L, CK-MB: 42 U/L, ALT: 339 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase: 398 U/L, hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase: 1080 U/L, and lactic dehydrogenase: 1151 U/L).
An ECG showed WPW syndrome, a high voltage in the left ventricle, and an inverted T wave at 13 years old (Figure 4b).
The boy was deprived of education owing to his intellectual disability.

people.zygosity_or_genotype: carrier; zygosity not stated (male, X-linked gene)
people.key_phenotypes: WPW; symmetric HCM with later LV dilation and LVEF 34% then 8%; attention deficit and learning difficulty; raised CK and liver enzymes; death from heart failure at 22

Four patients (4/7, 57.14%) presented with HCM phenotype, including two with symmetric patterns (Ⅲ-1 and Ⅲ-6; Figures 2A, 3A)

phenotype_specificity.statement: Authors describe case 1 as showing the classic triad, with autophagic vacuoles on biopsy; the 37215540 proband was diagnosed by electron microscopy and genetic testing. No paper reports testing of other genes or a negative panel/exome.

quotes.quote: These abnormal findings manifested with the classic triad of cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and intellectual disability in this patient.
An endomyocardial biopsy and electron microscopic examination showed autophagic vacuoles.
Subsequently, Danon disease was diagnosed at Beijing Union Hospital through electron microscopic examinations and genetic testing (13).

segregation.statement: 37215540: eight of fourteen family members in generations Ⅱ–Ⅳ carry the variant, including the proband; seven of them (five females, two males) are described as affected patients and Ⅳ-1 is an asymptomatic 8-year-old boy. The text does not list which eight people were genotyped as carriers, how many relatives were tested, or any tested non-carriers (pedigree figure only). Affected females show milder, later disease. 33530800 reports no relatives.

quotes.quote: Among the fourteen family members from generation Ⅱ–Ⅳ, eight individuals [including the proband (Ⅲ-1)] were confirmed to have frameshift mutation secondary to a 2-bp deletion (c.257_258delCC) in the exon 3 of the LAMP2 gene.
Seven patients (five females and two males), belonging to the same family and afflicted with DD, were enrolled in this study between 2017 and 2022.
CMR examination of Ⅳ-1, an asymptomatic 8-year-old boy, was failed due to lack of cooperation and subsequently excluded from the study.
I-1 died of heart disease at the age of 45.
None of the five female patients (Ⅱ-2, Ⅱ-3, Ⅲ-2, Ⅲ-4, and Ⅲ-5) exhibited substantial symptom deterioration.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-base deletion predicted to cause a frameshift, p.(Pro86GlnfsTer26) from the batch HGVS. 37215540 calls it a frameshift. Both papers state a loss-of-function / haploinsufficiency mechanism for the disease in general.

quotes.quote: Danon disease is a rare X-linked dominant genetic disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in the lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP-2) gene.
The haploinsufficiency of the X-linked LAMP2 gene in male patients, and the degree of skewed X inactivation in females lead to the sex-specific differences in clinical and CMR characteristics (4).

concerns: Probable same person across papers: 33530800 case 1 (DANON-ID0137) and 37215540 proband Ⅲ-1 (DANON-ID0232). Both papers come from the Affiliated Hospital of Jining Medical University with shared authors (Zhai Ning, Cui Yinghua); both men had WPW, were diagnosed at Beijing Union Hospital by electron microscopy and genetic testing, and died at 22-23. Case 1's lab ranges (AST 296-685, CK 1628-2423) include Ⅲ-1's values (AST 296, CK 1,960).

Contradictions if case 1 and Ⅲ-1 are the same man: age at death 23 vs 22; cause of death sudden cardiac arrest vs heart failure; an ICD received (33530800) vs ICD recommended but refused (37215540); first admission at 12 vs 14 years.

Probable same person: 33530800 case 2 (DANON-ID0138) and 37215540 Ⅲ-6 (not in the batch). Case 2's lab values (CK 1986, CK-MB 42, ALT 339, AST 398, HBDH 1080) match Ⅲ-6's Table 1 row (CK 1,986, CK-MB 42, ALT 338.9, AST 398, HBDH 1,080); both are boys with WPW and learning difficulty.

Carriers missing from the batch: 37215540 reports eight carriers, but the batch has only Ⅲ-1. The extraction holds variant rows for Ⅱ-2, Ⅱ-3, Ⅲ-2, Ⅲ-4, Ⅲ-5, Ⅲ-6 and Ⅳ-1 that are not batch rows. The text never assigns the variant to a named person other than Ⅲ-1.

37215540 contradicts itself on labels: 'Both IV-1 and IV-6 experienced cardiomyopathy with earlier onset' and 'low T2 signal foci ... of patient IV-1 and IV-6' seem to mean Ⅲ-1 and Ⅲ-6 (no Ⅳ-6 exists, and Ⅳ-1 had no CMR). It also lists Ⅲ-2 among adults with cardiomyopathy although Ⅲ-2 is 15 with normal morphology.

The proband may have been reported before: 37215540 cites Cheng et al. 2012 (PMID 22108829) for his diagnosis, and 33530800 cites Cheng & Fang 2012 (PMID 22261172) for case 1's ablation. Neither is in this batch.
No transcript, no protein change and no maternal carrier status are stated in the text. Zygosity is stated only for case 2.
37215540 is an imaging case series. Family relationships between carriers (e.g. who is Ⅲ-1's mother) are given only in the pedigree figure, not in the text.
notes_for_panel: Probably two or three distinct males from one Jining family (case 1 ≈ Ⅲ-1; case 2 ≈ Ⅲ-6), not three unrelated probands. Family evidence (eight carriers among 14 relatives) is in 37215540, but individual genotypes appear only in its pedigree figure.
